$note: CANONICAL BRAND VALUES. Nothing else in this repo may declare a colour. Edit here, then run `pnpm brand:tokens`. Rationale for every value lives in tokens.ts and drafts/brand/GUIDELINES.html.

illustration.$note: Guardrails for generated raster art (D17, 2026-08-12). No new hues — ground/ground-alt/ink alias the marketing values. Raster cannot be tokenised into CSS, so the real content here is the ceilings, which drafts/brand/art/build_art.py asserts against every shipped asset. This block is deliberately invisible to css(): it reaches tokens.generated.json only. Units: OKLCH chroma and OKLab distance, both x100.
illustration.$calibration: Measured against the real palette: sand 1.8, clay 2.7, espresso 4.1, royalblue 18.8, magenta 32.2. maxChroma 12 leaves headroom above espresso for photographic shadow and highlight while still rejecting any actual hue — 22 was the first draft and would have passed royalblue, which defeats the point. Sample screenshots are checked the OTHER way: they must have a brand colour of their OWN (p99 >= sampleMinChroma) rather than merely sit far from bone, because a light SaaS UI is only dE 2.9 from bone and a distance gate would have forced every sample dark or heavily tinted — less believable, which is the one thing a sample cannot afford to be.
